title: harborline-logistics-partner-scout
content:
Notes to self - Harborline Logistics (HL) prospect scout - quick brain dump

High level thesis
- Harborline = mid-market maritime/logistics operator focused on port ops, container tracking, and customs compliance. Heavy on legacy TMS integrations + lots of PDFs (BOLs, customs forms). Potential fit: Redwood Private or Dedicated for data residency, plus our Optimize features to reduce per-token cost for high-volume manifest text.
- Why partner? They have an existing product roadmap to add predictive ETA and automated exception triage; team is small; likely to prefer a vendor vs building NLU in-house.

Key contacts (pulled from LinkedIn + site)
- Priya Shah, Head of Platform (decision maker on platform partnerships) - priya@harborline.com (guess)
- Mark Elgin, CTO (security + infra sign-off)
- Nina Morales, Product Lead - Logistics Visibility (PM for ETA product)
- Jose Rivera, Ops (power user)
- Note: CTO previously at a fintech startup — may push back on hosted APIs for compliance.

Account context / stats to surface in outreach
- ~120 employees (engineering ~18)
- Operates in NA & EU; plans expansion into Chile & Panama in 2026 (regulatory pain points)
- Current infra: Postgres + ElasticSearch + on-prem SFTP for carriers; no standard vector DB in stack
- Volume estimate: 50–150k manifest documents/month (rough, from public job posts mentioning "tons of PDFs")

Pain & opportunity mapping 
- Pain #1: manual exception handling (90% of cases are routine but handled by humans). Opportunity: LLM-based triage to surface root cause, suggest message templates, auto-populate customs forms.
- Pain #2: long-tail document formats; each carrier uses different BOL structure. Opportunity: Redwood document ingestion + embeddings + retrieval to normalize and extract fields with high precision.
- Pain #3: latency & cost at scale. Opportunity: Redwood Optimize + batching + quantization profiles to hit sub-200ms p95 for short reply flows and keep cost predictable.

Pilot hypothesis (6-week POC) 
Objective: automated exception triage for one route (LA ports -> inland distribution)
Success metrics (example):
- triage accuracy >= 78% (vs human baseline)
- triage leads to 25% reduction in manual touches within pilot scope
- p95 latency for inference < 500ms for single-turn requests; cost <= $0.005 per inference average
Scope: 2 data sources (carrier BOL PDFs + internal incident tickets), 1 rule set for triage labels, integrated with Slack notifications.
Deliverables: 6-week runbook, weekly checkpoints, final report with token/cost analysis and rollout plan.
Commercial ask: 3-month Dedicated eval w/ usage cap; or hosted trial with data isolation + SOC2 add-on.

Outbound email drafts (variants)
Variant A - short (cold)\Subject: Reduce manual exception handling for Harborline\Hi Priya — quick note from Evan at Redwood Inference. We help logistics teams reduce manual exception triage by automating the first-pass diagnosis and suggested actions using a production-grade inference stack.
Would you be open to a 20-min call next week to see a short anonymized demo?
Thanks,
Evan

Variant B - value + social proof\Subject: 30% fewer manual touches on exceptions — short example\Hi Priya — saw Harborline expanding into Chile — congrats. We recently ran a pilot with a mid-market carrier that cut exception-handling touches by ~28% in 8 weeks using an LLM + retrieval pipeline and our Dedicated inference. No model-building required from their team.
Can I share a 6-week pilot plan tailored for Harborline? I can send a one-pager.
Evan

Cold call script (30–60s opener)\- Intro (10s): Evan Park, Redwood Inference — we provide production LLM serving + ops for teams building shipping/logistics features.\- Quick value (15s): We helped a similar customer automate first-pass exception triage and auto-populate customs forms, reducing manual work by ~25% and cutting per-event processing cost.\- Ask (5s): Is automating exceptions something on your roadmap this quarter? If yes: schedule 30m demo.

Objections & responses (prep)\Objection: "We can't send sensitive docs to hosted API."\- Response: Totally fair — we’ve done this via Redwood Private (VPC) and on-prem bundle; also support KM integrations (KMS/HSM) and have audit logs. For a pilot we can set up a dedicated environment.\Objection: "We already tried an LLM and it hallucinated / was unreliable."\- Response: Agree — hallucination is real. Our approach is retrieval-augmented generation + calibrated prompts + candidate reranking and built-in evals so we can quantify regressions vs baseline. We can show examples and the eval harness in the pilot.\Objection: "Cost at scale will be too high."\- Response: We optimize via batching, KV caching, quantized model variants and provide per-route cost dashboards. Pilot will include a cost plan and recommendations.

Integration ideas (engineering-friendly)\- Ingest pipeline: SFTP pickup -> OCR -> canonicalized JSON -> vectorize -> Redwood retrieval endpoint -> reranker -> structured output to ticketing system.\- Storage: Suggest starting with open-source vector DB they prefer (we're DB-agnostic) or our managed embeddings store if they want less ops.\- Latency expectations: for short triage flows aim for 150–300ms p50, 400–600ms p95 depending on sequence lengths and batching policy.

Pitch deck one-pager bullets to attach\- Who we are: production-first inference platform (hosted / dedicated / private)\- Value props: reliability (SLA + fallbacks), cost controls (Optimize), observability (per-token + per-route metrics)\- Pilot proposition: 6-week POC, defined success metrics, handover playbook\- Pricing anchors: Dedicated eval, then reserved capacity model (monthly commit)

Internal asks / TODOs\- Ask SE: Lina to prepare technical appendix: required infra, latency trade-offs, recommended quantization settings for LLMs used in triage. (Lina - can you draft by 2026-01-20?)\- Ask Legal: Samir to confirm acceptability of NDA + data processing addendum for pilot with EU operations. (Samir - pls flag any required clauses)\- Demo prep: Assemble small synthetic dataset (10–40 BOL PDFs + 100 tickets) we can use for anonymized demo. Where to host demo data? propose sandbox in Dedicated eval cluster.

Meeting prep checklist (first intro call)
- Confirm stakeholders and security constraints (Priya, Mark?)\- Ask about current ticket volume for exceptions and current SLA for resolution\- Ask what systems BOLs live in and if SFTP/OCR pipeline exists\- Ask about KPIs for "success" and timeline for rollout

Potential red flags\- Heavy legal/SaaS procurement that will elongate sales cycle (>6 months)\- Preference for closed-source internal models (they might prefer building vs buying)

Follow-ups / next steps\- Send tailored one-pager + pilot proposal after intro call\- Schedule SE deep-dive if security/infrastructure look favorable

Quick outreach cadence (if no reply)
- Day 0: cold email variant A\- Day 3: follow-up variant B w/ 1-pager\- Day 10: LinkedIn connection + short note\- Day 20: last attempt with customer story + ask for intro to product/ops

Random brainstorm notes (freeform)
- Explore co-marketing: joint webinar on "scaling exception automation for ports" if pilot succeeds\- Data product idea: normalized manifest outputs as a managed data feed (revenue share?)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc informal. Do not share raw notes w/ legal or prospect. Convert to a cleaned one-pager before sending.

End of file
